newsitem.title: USA: White House cautious on Ralston status.
newsitem.headline: White House cautious on Ralston status.

text.p: The White House said Thursday Gen. Joseph Ralston remains a leading candidate to become chairman of the military joint chiefs of staff despite an adulterous affair 13 years ago, but cautioned that no final decision has been made.

Ralston, a four-star Air Force officer, is "an outstanding soldier and an outstanding vice chairman who has outstanding qualifications for the job, but the recommendation has not yet gone to the president," spokeswoman Anne Luzzatto said.

Defense officials said Ralston has been Defense Secretary William Cohen's favorite for the top military post but that Marine Corps Gen. John Sheehan, head of the Atlantic Command in Norfolk, Va., is also high on the list of candidates.

Luzzatto said Cohen had discussed Ralston's past sexual relationship with a woman not his wife, the latest in a series of such disclosures that have caused an upheaval in the military ranks, and that "he remains a candidate."
"The recommendation has yet to be made and the president will make his decision," she said.

A source close to the situation said Luzzatto's comments should not be read as a White House effort to distance itself from the officer while waiting to see how the political wind blows on the latest disclosure. Clinton's decision "is not expected to come for another week or so, so its proceeding apace," the source said.
